chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid altogether from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Habib al-Khath'ami who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Incumbent upon you is piety and diligence, and attend the funerals, and visit the sick, and be present in your mosques with your people, and love for the people what you love for yourselves. Is the man among you not ashamed that his neighbor knows his right while he does not know the right of his neighbor?'

key_terms.الاجتهاد: Ijtihad in this context means personal diligence and effort in religious practice, not legal reasoning
key_terms.الجنائز: Al-jana'iz — plural of janaza, referring to funeral prayers and processions
key_terms.الورع: Wara' — scrupulous piety, abstaining from anything doubtful or disliked by God
key_terms.حق الجار: Haqq al-jar — the right of the neighbor, a well-established Islamic concept with detailed rulings

ai.seo_question: What duties does Imam Sadiq prescribe for social relations with neighbors and community?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) exhorts his followers to a comprehensive program of personal piety and communal engagement. He commands five social duties — attending funerals, visiting the sick, worshipping communally in mosques, embodying the golden rule, and being conscientious about neighborly rights. The closing rhetorical question about the neighbor's rights was directed at early Shia communities who may have been tempted to withdraw from broader social life; the Imam emphasizes that true piety expresses itself through community.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, and Muhammad Bin Khalid, altogether from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Habeeb Al Khash’amy who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘(It is) upon you with the piety, and the striving, and attending the funerals, and consoling the sick, and to be present along with your people in the Masjids, and loving for the people what you are loving for yourselves. Would not the man from you be embarrassed if his neighbour were to recognise his right while he does not recognise the right of his neighbour?’
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al- Husayn ibn Sa’id and Muhammad ibn Khalid all from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Habib al-Khath’ami who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘You must maintain restraint from worldly attractions (sins), maintain persistence in work, attend funerals, and visit people during their illness. You should attend the Mosque with your own people, and love for people what you love for yourselves. Would it not be embarrassing for one of you to see that a neighbor recognizes your rights but you do not recognize the rights of your neighbor?”’
